title: Ajisai MCP result
description: One envelope for every Ajisai MCP tool result (compute, check, infer_contracts, outcomes, word_contract). `status` separates the three outcomes the boundary keeps distinct: a successful run (which includes a reason-carrying NIL), an Ajisai language error carrying its diagnosis, and a failure of the host rather than of the program. An optional field carrying no value is omitted rather than sent as `null`, so `diagnosis`, `aiDiagnostic` and `message` are simply absent from a plain success, and `contractDecls` from a source that declares no contract — test for presence, not for `null`. The text content block of a tool result carries this same object serialized, so a text-only client receives the whole result and not a summary of it.

stackElided.description: Present when the stack was too large to send in full and the values of the slots that do not fit a byte budget were dropped; this record says which. On an `error` the budget is the fixed one every error report applies (`errorStackBudget`): the report's answer is its diagnosis, and the stack is residual state. On an `ok` it is the agent profile's stack budget (`valueStackBudget`): the values that fit arrive whole, and an oversized one arrives as this record rather than the whole result being refused as `responseTooLarge`, so a caller learns what it left on the stack and can fix the program. Absent whenever nothing was dropped, which is every ordinary result.

slots.description: One entry per dropped slot, in stack order.

index.description: Position in `stack` and `stackDisplay`. Slots keep their index: a dropped slot is replaced in place, never removed, so a diagnosis that points at stack depth still points at the same thing.

approxBytes.description: Roughly what the slot would have serialized to, counted without building the text.

elements.description: Direct children, for a collection. Absent for a leaf.

outcome.description: compute only. Which of the language’s three results (LANG.FAILURE) the run produced, as a spec/outcomes.json id: `value`, `nil:<reason>` for a reasoned absence on top of the stack (still `status: ok`), or `error:<category>` for a language ERROR (`status: error`). The same ids the `outcomes` tool predicts, so a run is checked against a prediction with one membership test. Absent only when the result cannot be classified (an unlabelled NIL, an error naming no category).

outcomes.description: outcomes only. Every outcome id the program could produce, sorted; the actual run’s `outcome` is always a member.

exact.description: outcomes only. True exactly when `outcomes` holds one id — the single outcome the program produces (an empty program, or source that does not tokenize or balance its brackets). False means a sound superset, never a wrong answer.

limitProfile.description: outcomes only. The resource ceilings the prediction assumed, keyed like the `limits` of `ajisai://limits`.

partiality.description: The registry's derivation over the Words the body calls: `projecting` when one can answer a reasoned NIL of its own, `partial` when one can raise on operands of the right kind, `total` otherwise.

field.description: LANG.CONTRACT.FIELD: `leaving` when the body can answer a point over zero (`1/0` `-1/0` `0/0`) from operands holding none — it calls DIV, POW or NUM, writes a literal over zero, or runs code the inference cannot read — and `closed` otherwise, in which case the field laws hold over finite operands. A `DIV` by a finite non-zero literal or a `POW` to a finite non-negative literal exponent stays `closed`.

fieldExits.description: Where a `leaving` body leaves the field, in body order: the Words it calls there and the literals it writes over zero. Empty for a `closed` body.

suggested.description: A paste-ready `#:contract` line for this Word, written in the keys and values of this same object, so pasting it back verifies exactly what was reported.

contracts.description: Inferred contracts for the user-defined Words in the submitted source (`infer_contracts` only). Every key a registered Word's contract also has (`word_contract`, and `CONTRACT` inside the language) is spelled the same and takes the same values, so an inferred and a registered contract compare directly. Reports each cost axis as its class alone; exactness is observable through `suggested`, which names only the axes the declaration checker can verify.

errorFlowTraceElided.description: Present when the trace's events did not all fit its byte budget (the same 64 KiB an error report's stack gets): the first events that fit half of it and the last that fit the other half are sent in `errorFlowTrace`, in order, and this record says how many between them were dropped. Absent whenever the whole trace was sent.

aiDiagnostic.description: On an `error`, its classification — and only that: the checks, candidates and ceiling facts are `diagnosis`'s, the report's one copy. A NIL never appears here; its reason is the value's `semantics.absence.reason`.

category.description: The spec/outcomes.json error category — the id `outcome` names as `error:<category>`.

repair.description: Present exactly when spec/outcomes.json marks the category `repair: program`: the program is what to change. Absent, as in the registry, means an operand is what is wrong.

family.description: The failing Word's spec/words.json family, when a Core Word is at fault.

resourceUsage.description: What this run spent of the budgets that could have refused it. Every key names a ceiling of the `ajisai://limits` profile (`mcp.limitProfile`) and carries the same number the ceiling compared against — read from the counter the check reads, not a parallel copy — so an agent can subtract one from the other and know what it has left. Only the accumulating ceilings appear: `bigintBits` and `algebraicTerms` are checked per result and never accumulated, so there is no peak to report and none is invented.

numericWork.description: Internal arithmetic work charged, in limb-multiply units, against the `numericWork` ceiling.

collectionWork.description: Element operations charged inside collection Words — copies, order comparisons and equality probes — against the `collectionWork` ceiling. Priced from the operand, so an element that is wide, nested or algebraic costs more than a machine word; a collection Word loops inside one execution step, so this is the only counter that can see it.

receipt.description: compute only. The execution receipt (rust/src/agent/execution_receipt.rs): `digest` is a BLAKE3 over the source, the engine version, the registry digest, the limit profile, the outcome status, the observation digest and the resource usage. This adapter sends the three inputs nothing else in the envelope carries — `digest`, `sourceDigest`, `registryDigest` — and a verifier takes the rest from beside them: `status`, `observationDigest`, `resourceUsage`, `mcp.engineVersion`, and the engine-side entries of `ajisai://limits` as the limit profile. The native CLI's `--json` receipt carries them all inline.

registrySchemaVersion.description: Schema version of the packaged Word registry (`word_contract` only). Distinct from the envelope's own `schemaVersion`.

matches.description: Canonical registry entries matching the requested Word (`word_contract` only).

suggestions.description: Registry names closest to an unmatched request, best match first (`word_contract` only). Empty whenever `matches` is non-empty.

serverVersion.description: Version of this MCP adapter — a separate component from the Ajisai engine below it. A stored result names both, so a missing field can be told apart from a field this adapter version never sent.

assetDigest.description: SHA-256 of the Word registry file this adapter packages (assets/words.json), checked against assets/metadata.json at startup. It identifies the adapter's asset, not the engine's registry: the engine's own `receipt.registryDigest` is a BLAKE3 digest over words and outcomes, in `#`-prefixed form, and the two are not comparable.

backend.description: Which of the two interchangeable backends answered. They are semantically equivalent — `backend/parity-test.js` asserts it case by case — so this identifies the execution path for auditing, not a difference in meaning.

limitProfile.description: The name of the host profile applied to this call — the `profile` of the `ajisai://limits` resource, which carries the twelve ceilings themselves. They are constants of the server, so they travel once, in that resource, rather than on every result; a ceiling that fires names itself and its value in `diagnosis.resourceLimit`, and a host failure about one names it in `error.limit`. Every entry is pinned by a case in `golden/limits.json`.

hostError.description: A failure of the host, never of the Ajisai program. `code` is the stable identifier to branch on; `message` is safe to show a model and deliberately carries no host paths, environment-variable names or spawn detail.

limit.description: The declared ceiling (an entry of `ajisai://limits`) this failure is about, when it is about one.

debugCheck.description: One repair step. Match on `code`; `title` and `detail` are display text and may be reworded or gain locales.

resourceLimitFacts.description: Which declared ceiling a resource-limit failure crossed, or a generative Word declined a result under (the diagnosis of a NIL(spaceExhausted), which can name `materializedElements`). `resource` names an entry of the `ajisai://limits` profile, and `limit` is its value, so no result needs the profile read to be acted on. `observed` is what crossed it — a real measured size for the size ceilings, but for a cumulative work ceiling only the budget spent at the moment of refusal, which sits a hair over `limit` however far over the request was. Where that is so, `progress` carries the number to act on instead.

progress.description: How far an operation charged as it goes had got when its budget ran out. Present only where `observed` cannot say how much smaller the input must be; absent for every ceiling whose `observed` is a real size. `completed` is the answer rather than a hint at it: the budget bought exactly that many units of this data, so retrying with that many is what fits.

where.description: The locus the diagnosis is about: a Core Word, a User Word the live dictionary holds, or a name that resolved to nothing.

candidates.description: Known Words closest to an unrecognized name, best match first. Empty for every other cause class.

wordContract.description: One canonical entry of the generated `spec/words.json` registry, reproduced verbatim.

cost.description: What the Word charges on each of the three metered resources the runtime counts (`executionSteps` / `numericWork` / `collectionWork`). The classes join pointwise under concatenation, so a phrase's bound on an axis is the widest class any of its Words declares there — which is what lets a caller budget a program without running it.

exactTerm.description: One term c·√m of the normal form: the rational coefficient numerator/denominator and the square-free radicand m (1 for the rational term).

protocolNode.description: One stack value as observed at the host boundary. Every field is derived from the value itself, never from the Word that produced it (LANG.VALUES.DENOTATION). A vector's own elements are observedValue nodes in turn (see `value` below), so this definition is recursive.

type.description: The value's domain (LANG.VALUES.DISJOINT), discriminating `value`'s shape. A NIL is `nil` wherever it stands, including in truth position, where it reads as UNKNOWN (LANG.VALUES.TRUTH).

value.description: Shape depends on `type`: nil -> null; boolean -> boolean; number -> {numerator, denominator} (arbitrary-precision decimal strings, the pair reduced and the denominator non-negative: zero exactly for the three points over zero, `1/0`, `-1/0`, `0/0`, LANG.VALUES.EXACT); string or symbol -> string (a symbol's bare name); vector -> an array of observedValue; record -> {keys, values}, two arrays of observedValue of equal length, aligned position by position (LANG.RECORDS.STRUCTURE). null for any type when `elided` is present.

costAxis.description: A sound upper bound on one metered resource. `class` bounds how the charge grows with the Word's input; `exact` records that some contribution provably attains it, rather than the bound being a safe over-approximation.

protocolSemantics.description: Present on every node, a Vector nested in a Vector included: how a value is stored does not decide what its node says (LANG.AUTHORITY.FREEDOM). Every field is optional. Both host surfaces emit the same set, because both render it with one function (rust/src/agent/report.rs::semantics_json).

truthValue.description: Present on a Boolean node, and only there (rust/src/types/value_absence.rs::truth_value). UNKNOWN is a NIL (LANG.VALUES.TRUTH) and is observed through `absence`, not here.

approximate.description: true when the node is an irrational scalar (LANG.VALUES.EXACT), whose `value` is therefore a rational approximation: the best convergent the observation budget affords, or, for a value too large to afford even one, a term-by-term one. `exactTerms` is the value. Never present otherwise.

exactTerms.description: An irrational scalar's exact multiquadratic normal form, structured for computation: one term per {numerator, denominator, radicand}. The stack display writes the same terms as one token (`sqrt(2)`, `1/1+sqrt(2)`).

protocolAbsence.description: Present only on a nil-type node. `reason` is the stable, machine-readable identifier LANG.VALUES.NIL calls the entire observable content of a NIL (one of spec/outcomes.json's NIL reasons); it is absent only for a NIL an implementation could not yet label. `detail` is the text a `userDeclared` reason carries, which is part of that reason. `origin` and `recoverability` are diagnostic state beyond the reason, informational only: a program cannot observe them, and two NILs with one reason are one value whatever their origin. `diagnosis` nests the structured diagnosis object docs/dev/agent-cli-output-contract.md describes, when the runtime produced one.

protocolElided.description: Present only in the stack of a CLI/MCP agent report, on a slot whose value was dropped to keep the report deliverable (rust/src/agent/error_stack.rs): under the fixed error budget every error report applies (`errorStackBudget`), or under the stack budget a host chose for successful results (`valueStackBudget`, the agent profile's; the trusted profile sets none). `type` and `semantics` still describe what the value was (less an algebraic value's `exactTerms`, whose count moves here); `value` is null. Tell it apart from a genuine NIL by `type`, which names the real domain, and by this field's presence.

protocolTruncated.description: Present only in the playground's stack view (AjisaiInterpreter.collect_stack, rust/src/agent/stack_view.rs), on a vector cut to its first 100 elements, the most the playground draws of one collection; never in a CLI/MCP agent report. `value` holds those leading elements, each a full observedValue (cut in turn if it is a long vector). This field describes what was left out, so a host decides from the view what it would decide from the whole value: `length` is the vector's element count; `holdsNil` and `holdsRecord` say whether a NIL or a Record sits anywhere in the left-out elements; `digest` is a 64-bit hash of the left-out elements under value equality, so the views of two different values differ. Presentation only: the value on the stack stays whole.
